title: The lighthouse keeper's notebook
summary: Marta finds a hidden notebook and learns something about her quiet grandfather.
paragraphs: Marta was sixteen when she found the notebook. It was hidden behind a loose {{brick}} in her grandfather's kitchen, {{wrapped}} in an old blue scarf. She only noticed it because the brick moved when she leaned against the wall to tie her shoe.

Inside, every page had the same three things: the date, the weather and one short sentence. "Strong wind. A fishing boat came home late." "Fog all day. Nobody visited." "Calm sea. Saw dolphins near the rocks." The first page was from 1971. The last one was from the year Marta was born.

Her grandfather had been the {{lighthouse}} keeper for forty years, but he never talked about it. When people asked, he just smiled and changed the subject. Marta had always thought he was {{bored}} with the job. Now she wasn't so sure.

She took the notebook to him in the garden. For a long moment he didn't say anything. Then he turned the pages slowly, and she saw that his eyes were wet. "I thought I had lost this," he said. "Your grandmother gave it to me. She said that if I wrote one true thing every day, the lonely nights would feel shorter."

That evening, Marta {{climbed}} the narrow stairs to the top of the lighthouse for the first time. The lamp had not worked for years, but the {{view}} was amazing: the whole bay, the village and the boats coming in. She sat down, opened the notebook at a new page and wrote the date, the weather and one sentence of her own.

brick.meaning: a hard block of baked clay used to build walls

wrapped.meaning: covered completely in paper or cloth

lighthouse.meaning: a tower by the sea with a strong light to guide ships

climbed.meaning: went up something, often using your hands and feet

view.meaning: everything you can see from a place

questions.question: Why did Marta find the notebook?
options: She was looking for something to read.
A brick moved when she leaned on the wall.
Her grandfather asked her to find it.
It fell out of a scarf in the garden.
questions.explanation: The brick moved when she leaned against the wall to tie her shoe.

questions.question: What did each page of the notebook contain?
options: A long story about the sea
A list of the boats that came in
The date, the weather and one sentence
questions.explanation: Every page had the date, the weather and one short sentence.

questions.question: Why did her grandfather start writing in the notebook?
options: He had to write a report for his job.
His wife told him it would make lonely nights feel shorter.
He wanted to remember the names of the fishermen.
He was bored and had nothing else to do.
questions.explanation: His wife gave him the notebook and said one true thing a day would make the nights feel shorter.

questions.question: How did Marta's opinion of her grandfather's job change?
options: She decided the job was dangerous.
She still thought he was bored.
She was no longer sure that he had been bored.
She thought he had wanted a different job.
questions.explanation: She had always thought he was bored, but after reading the notebook she wasn't so sure.
